findings.detail: Uses db.WithTx for transactional label addition, ensuring atomicity
deleteIssueLabel checks count==0 and returns nil if label wasn't attached, making it safe to retry
Uses db.WithTx for atomic replace operation
Uses db.WithTx but long-running transaction with N deletes + N inserts + N updates could cause lock contention
findings.recommendation: Consider batch operations to reduce transaction duration

endpoint_resiliency.cascading_failure_risk: Long transaction could block other label operations on same issue

findings.detail: Pure DB read with pagination, no external calls
Duplicate key detection prevents double-creation (returns 422 on retry)
findings.recommendation: None needed - safe to retry, will get clear error

findings.detail: DB deletion and authorized_keys rewrite are separate operations. If rewrite fails after DB delete, the key is removed from DB but still in authorized_keys (or vice versa on partial failure)
findings.recommendation: Consider making the rewrite failure non-fatal or adding a recovery mechanism

findings.detail: SSHOpLocker mutex serializes all SSH key operations globally. A slow rewrite blocks all other key operations
findings.recommendation: Consider async rewrite with eventual consistency

non_atomic_operations: DB delete + filesystem rewrite are not atomic - partial failure leaves inconsistent state
endpoint_resiliency.cascading_failure_risk: SSHOpLocker contention can block all SSH key operations if rewrite is slow
endpoint_resiliency.graceful_degradation: If key not found, silently succeeds (no-op)

rate_limiting.detail: No rate limiting on these endpoints
rate_limiting.recommendation: Consider rate limiting deploy key creation to prevent abuse

dead_letter_queues.detail: No async flows in these endpoints

single_points_of_failure: authorized_keys file - single file rewritten on every key change
cascading_failure_paths: SSHOpLocker contention → all key operations blocked during rewrite
